title: Study of Two Ternary Al-Mg-Zn Systems Used as Electrical Conductors
content: Within the aluminum alloys, the 7XXX series stands out due to their high mechanical strength and wide application in aircraft and automobile industries. The strength of these alloys is attributed to the formation of finer and homogeneously dispersed precipitates in the Al matrix, produced by the T6 heat treatment, which involves solubilization, cooling, and aging processing [1]. Another route by which aluminum alloys are hardened is plastic deformation, which introduces internal stresses and dislocations in the Al matrix [2]. Both hardening processes have a favorable effect on the mechanical properties of the material; however, very few studies have investigated the correlation between cold plastic deformation and the formation of precipitates on the mechanical properties and electrical conductivity of these alloys [3].
